safety_policy.permission_rule: A location being outside a mapped protected area does not grant permission. Show active steps only when the land or waterbody manager has explicitly authorised removal at that site.
safety_policy.model_rule: The vision model produces a candidate identification, not an official botanical confirmation. Low-confidence or ambiguous results must remain observation-only.
safety_policy.protected_land_rule: On protected land, or whenever protection or permission is uncertain, users must not touch, collect, cut or remove the plant. They may photograph safely and submit a candidate report.
never_recommend: chainsaws, powered cutters or heavy machinery
entering water, unstable banks, steep slopes or dense thorny thickets
decision_logic: If model confidence is below the product threshold or the user selects 'not sure', show identification checks and reporting only.
If protected status is true, unknown or unavailable, show the protected/permission-unknown path.
If removal permission is not explicitly confirmed, show the protected/permission-unknown path even when the map says the place is not protected.
If guidance_mode is report_only, never show physical removal steps.
If guidance_mode is site_manager_confirmation_required, show active steps only when the coordinator has marked that species as a target for that site.
Otherwise show the authorised-site path, including its eligibility and stop conditions.

authorised_site.title: Beginner-safe action on an authorised site
authorised_site.eligibility: Only a small seedling that can be removed without a saw, ladder or powered tool, and only after explicit land-manager approval.

steps.text: Wear gloves. If pods are present, place the pods in a bag before touching the seedling.
When soil is moist, grip the seedling low and pull steadily so the whole root comes out.
Place the whole seedling and any loose pods in a durable bag for disposal according to the site manager's instructions.

stop_conditions.text: Stop and report if the stem is woody, the plant is taller than the user, pods are opening, or the root will not lift easily.

spread_prevention.text: Do not move soil containing seeds to another site; seed can be transported by water and machinery.
Inspect gloves, footwear and tools and remove any pods or seeds before leaving.

do_not_do.text: Do not cut or ring-bark mature shrubs or trees; cutting can leave a resprouting stump and is not a beginner task.
Do not burn plant material or apply herbicide through this app.

follow_up.text: Recheck the exact point after 4–6 weeks and again after rain for seedlings or stump regrowth.

spread_prevention.text: Inspect socks, trousers, shoelaces, gloves and bags for barbed seeds before leaving the point.

do_not_do.text: Do not remove it merely because the classifier recognises it; its Malaysian status is naturalised, not nationally invasive.

follow_up.text: Revisit in 3–4 weeks and remove new target seedlings before they flower, if the site manager continues the programme.

steps.text: Wear gloves and work when soil is moist. Grip near the base and pull out the root crown and roots.

Bag flower or seed heads before moving the rest of the plant.

spread_prevention.text: Do not leave broken stems on moist soil because vegetative pieces can regrow.

do_not_do.text: Do not slash or burn it; damaged plants can regrow and fire is not a beginner control method.
Do not attempt a dense or flowering stand.

follow_up.text: Photograph the cleared point and recheck it after 4–6 weeks for root-crown regrowth or seedlings.

steps.text: Wear gloves and work from a stable dry edge. Lift the entire rosette, attached daughter plants and roots together.
Collect every loose fragment visible within safe reach; small pieces left in water can continue spreading.
Drain the plants in a contained tub or on an impermeable surface away from drains and waterways, then bag or dispose of them as the manager directs.

stop_conditions.text: Stop if the patch forms a mat, is beyond arm's reach, or requires entering water.

spread_prevention.text: Never return roots, daughter plants or broken pieces to the water.
Rinse or brush mud and plant fragments from tools only in a contained place away from drains and natural water.

do_not_do.text: Do not wade, swim, use a boat or stand on an unstable bank.
Do not release removed plants into another pond, drain or stream.

follow_up.text: Recheck the same shoreline after 1–2 weeks because overlooked daughter plants can drift back.

spread_prevention.text: Do not leave any stem section with a node on moist ground; one-node fragments can root.

do_not_do.text: Do not pull vines from trees, steep banks or overhead growth.
Do not mow or slash a small patch into fragments.

follow_up.text: Recheck after 2–4 weeks and photograph any regrowth from missed nodes or the root base.

authorised_site.title: Beginner-safe action on an authorised site
authorised_site.eligibility: Only a tiny isolated seedling before flowering or pod formation, reachable without entering a thicket, and with site permission.

steps.text: Wear thick gloves, long sleeves, long trousers and closed shoes because the stems carry hooked prickles.
When soil is moist, grip the seedling low using gloved hands and pull out the whole root.
Place it directly into a strong bag so prickles and any unnoticed seed do not catch on clothing.

stop_conditions.text: Stop if there are flowers, pods, multiple intertwined stems or a patch larger than one isolated seedling.

spread_prevention.text: Do not move soil from the plant's base; seed can spread with soil, water, vehicles and machinery.
Inspect clothing, laces, gloves, tools and bags for prickles or pods before leaving.

do_not_do.text: Do not enter or pull a tangled patch and do not slash a seeding plant.
Do not handle it with bare hands.

follow_up.text: Recheck after 3–4 weeks and after heavy rain because dormant seed may produce new seedlings.

stop_conditions.text: Always stop at observation and reporting; there is no public removal workflow for this class.

spread_prevention.text: Avoid walking or driving through a patch; seed can move in mud and on vehicles, boats, machinery and clothing.
Clean any mud from footwear or equipment at the approved cleaning point before visiting another wetland.

do_not_do.text: Do not cut, pull, enter or burn the thicket.
Do not collect pods or carry branches as samples.

follow_up.text: A coordinator should schedule expert assessment and repeat photographs from the same safe point.

spread_prevention.text: Do not brush against flowering plants or carry any part on clothing.

authorised_site.title: Beginner-safe action on an authorised site
authorised_site.eligibility: Only a small isolated plant explicitly designated by the site manager, before seed segments are shedding, and only if it can be hand-pulled without cutting a woody stem.

steps.text: Wear gloves. If dry fruit is present, enclose and bag the fruiting tips before moving the stem.
Pull from low on the stem when soil is moist, removing the whole root.
Place the plant and every fruit segment into a durable closed bag.

stop_conditions.text: Stop if fruit is shedding, the stem is woody, or there is more than a small isolated patch.

spread_prevention.text: Inspect clothes, socks, animal fur, tools and muddy footwear because the awned fruit segments can hitchhike.
Do not move contaminated hay, soil or mud to another site.

do_not_do.text: Do not cut a mature woody plant or slash a seeding patch.
Do not remove it without local target confirmation; Malaysia-wide IAS status is unresolved in this dataset.

follow_up.text: Recheck after 4 weeks and after rain for seedlings or regrowth.
